profile.title: Co-investment
profile.description: Private discovery of co-investment counterparties: a follower with a ticket range and sector scope seeks rounds with a committed institutional lead, without announcing that it is deploying.

sector.subject: preference
sector.description: Sectors the Principal accepts. A general value is an accepted set: holding the whole list means any sector is acceptable.

geography.subject: preference
geography.description: Holding `europe` accepts every European geography (accepted_set), so a claim on `france` answers compatible.

ticket_eur.subject: preference
ticket_eur.description: The Principal's investable range per deal. Typically evaluation_only in the holder's Disclosure Policy; the manifest types it, the Principal protects it.

lead_commitment_eur.subject: requirement
lead_commitment_eur.description: Minimum committed institutional lead the follower requires in the round. A condition on the counterparty's round, not a property of the holder.

joint_predicates.name: ticket_meets
joint_predicates.semantics: There exists a single ticket amount acceptable to both sides: inside the follower's investable range AND inside the allocation the round offers. Overlap of each private range with an asked range proves nothing (a follower capped at 80k and a round requiring 90k minimum both overlap 50k-100k). On the wire: each side asks the other `ticket_eur compatible_with <amount>`, the amount being a candidate allocation on the lattice, never either side's private bound; each responder answers whether that one amount lies inside its own private range. The predicate holds when both directions answered `compatible` to the same amount.

qualification.opportunity_meaning: A qualified Opportunity asserts that sector, geography, stage, ticket range and lead commitment were each examined and found compatible -- or, for a value its holder keeps evaluation-only, conditionally compatible, and then listed in open_conditions; that the lead commitment met the follower's floor as the round's Agent answered it (an answer, not an attestation: no claim proves a commitment exists); and that ticket_meets held for at least one candidate amount answered in both directions. It asserts nothing about terms, valuation or the parties' identities.
